intro: Cooking, laying the table and telling what goes wrong with «se me ha…».
p.freír.consejo: It is irregular: «frío», «fríe». The i carries an accent in «freír» and in «frío».
p.hervir.consejo: It changes e to ie: «hierve», «hiervo». The h is silent and the v sounds like b.
p.asar.consejo: You roast in the oven: «pollo asado». Do not mix it up with «azar», which is chance.
p.batir.consejo: You whisk eggs. It is also used in «batir un récord»: beating the best result.
p.pelar.consejo: You peel potatoes, oranges and apples. It is a regular verb: «pelo», «pelas».
p.horno.consejo: The h is silent: OR-no. You say «en el horno».
p.mantel.consejo: The stress is at the end: man-TEL. No accent. The plural is «manteles».
p.servilleta.consejo: The v sounds like b and the ll like y: ser-bi-YE-ta.
p.cubiertos.consejo: It is almost always plural: «los cubiertos». They go at the sides of the plate.
p.poner la mesa.consejo: You say «poner», not «hacer»: «pongo la mesa». The opposite is «quitar la mesa».
p.quemarse.consejo: With «se me ha quemado» the burnt thing is the subject: «se me han quemado las patatas».
p.en su punto.consejo: It is said about meat: «poco hecha», «en su punto», «muy hecha». «En su punto» is the middle.
p.comida casera.consejo: It comes from «casa». A «persona casera» is someone who prefers to stay at home.
p.aliñar.consejo: The ñ sounds «ny»: a-li-NYAR. You dress a salad with oil, vinegar and salt.
b1.titulo: In the kitchen and at the table
b1.texto:
In the kitchen: **freír** (in oil), **hervir** (in water), **asar** (in the oven), **batir** eggs, **pelar** potatoes, **aliñar** a salad.

To **poner la mesa**: the **mantel**, the **servilletas**, the plates, the glasses and the **cubiertos**.

To tell about an accident without blaming anyone: **se me ha quemado** la cena, **se me ha caído** un plato. The thing is the subject and the person goes in **me / te / le / nos / os / les**.

Meat can be **poco hecha**, **en su punto** or **muy hecha**.
b2.f0.texto: Six people are coming for dinner.
b2.f1.texto: I've burnt the chicken by accident.
b2.f2.texto: We'll put some fish in the oven.
b2.f4.texto: Whisk the eggs for the omelette and dress the salad.
b2.f5.texto: Do I dress it with oil and vinegar?
b2.f6.texto: Taste the soup to see if it is bland.
b2.f8.texto: Where are the tablecloth and the glasses?
b2.f9.texto: They are in the bottom drawer.
b4.texto:
To say that something happens by accident, we use **se** + **me / te / le / nos / os / les** + verb:

- **Se me ha quemado** la cena.
- **Se me ha caído** un plato.
- **Se me han olvidado** las servilletas.

The thing that burns, falls or is forgotten is the **subject**: the verb agrees with it (**ha quemado**, **han olvidado**).

The pronoun **me** says who suffers the accident. With **haber**, the participle does not change: se me han olvidado.
b4.e0.texto: I've dropped a plate by accident.
b4.e1.texto: You've burnt the potatoes by accident.
b5.f0.texto: A grey smoke rises from the oven and fills the kitchen with a burnt smell.
b5.f1.texto: Lucía opens the window and shakes a white cloth in the air.
b5.f2.texto: The chicken rests on the tray, black as coal.
b5.f3.texto: Omar laughs out loud and gives her a pat on the shoulder.
b5.f4.texto: Between the two of them they put fresh fish on a dish and slide it into the oven.
b5.f5.texto: The guests arrive with flowers, with wine and with a huge appetite.
b5.f6.texto: On the table, a blue checked tablecloth holds six plates and six glasses.
b5.f7.texto: The napkins look like little white candles beside each plate.
b5.f8.texto: The fish comes out of the oven golden and juicy.
b5.f9.texto: The dinner ends amid laughter and with full glasses.
b6.o0.refuerzo: That's it! With «haber» the participle always ends in -o: ha quemado.
b6.o1.refuerzo: With «haber» the participle does not change gender, even if la cena is feminine.
b6.o2.refuerzo: After «ha» you need a participle, not the infinitive.
b6.pregunta: With «haber» the participle does not change. Which form is missing?
b7.o0.refuerzo: «Hervir» means cooking in boiling water, not in the oven.
b7.o1.refuerzo: «Aliñar» means putting oil and salt on a salad.
b7.o2.refuerzo: Well done! You roast in the oven: pollo asado.
b7.pregunta: How do you cook a chicken in the oven?
b8.frase: Bate los huevos y aliña la ensalada
b8.traduccion: Whisk the eggs and dress the salad
b9.o0.refuerzo: That's it! «Servilletas» is plural, and «han» agrees with it.
b9.o1.refuerzo: «Ha» is singular, but «las servilletas» is plural.
b9.o2.refuerzo: «He» is for «yo». The subject here is not «yo», it is las servilletas.
b9.pregunta: The subject is plural: las servilletas. Which form is missing?
b10.pregunta: Write in Spanish: «I've burnt dinner by accident.»
b11.o0.refuerzo: Yes! «Muy hecha» means well cooked, nothing pink.
b11.o1.refuerzo: «Poco hecha» is almost raw: the opposite of what you want.
b11.o2.refuerzo: «En su punto» is the middle, not well cooked.
b11.pregunta: You prefer your meat well cooked. How do you ask for it?
b12.o0.refuerzo: The expression is not «hacer la mesa». You say «poner».
b12.o1.refuerzo: Well done! You say «poner la mesa».
b12.pregunta: You get the plates and glasses ready. Which verb is missing?
p.vienen.consejo: Form of «venir»: the e becomes «ie». The v sounds like b: BYE-nen.
p.quemado.consejo: Participle of «quemar». The qu sounds k: ke-MA-do. With «haber» it does not change.
p.ponemos.consejo: Form of «poner» for «nosotros». Only the «yo» form is irregular: «pongo».
p.bate.consejo: Command with «tú» of «batir»: «bate los huevos». It also exists as the «él» form.
p.aliña.consejo: Command with «tú» of «aliñar». The ñ sounds «ny»: a-LI-nya.
p.aliño.consejo: Form of «aliñar» for «yo». The ñ sounds «ny»: a-LI-nyo. «¿Aliño con aceite?» asks for advice.
p.vinagre.consejo: The v sounds like b and the g is hard before r: bi-NA-gre. It is masculine: «el vinagre».
p.copas.consejo: The singular is «la copa». It is a glass with a stem, for wine for example.
p.cajón.consejo: The j sounds h and the stress is at the end: ka-HÓN. The plural is «cajones».
p.abajo.consejo: The j sounds h: a-BA-ho. The opposite is «arriba». «El cajón de abajo» is the bottom drawer.
p.caído.consejo: Participle of «caer». The accent splits a-í: ka-Í-do. In «se me ha caído» it does not change.
p.olvidado.consejo: Participle of «olvidar». The v sounds like b: ol-bi-DA-do. With «haber» it does not change.
p.servilletas.consejo: The singular is «la servilleta». The v sounds like b and the ll like y: ser-bi-YE-tas.
p.humo.consejo: The h is silent: U-mo. It is masculine: «el humo».
p.sacude.consejo: Form of «sacudir». The c before u sounds k: sa-KU-de.
p.paño.consejo: The ñ sounds «ny»: PA-nyo. It is masculine: «un paño».
p.carbón.consejo: The stress is at the end: kar-BÓN. «Negro como el carbón» means very black.
p.palmada.consejo: It comes from «palma», the palm of the hand. «Dar una palmada» is to pat.
p.meten.consejo: Form of «meter». «Meter en el horno» means to put into the oven.
p.invitados.consejo: The v sounds like b: in-bi-TA-dos. The singular is «el invitado». It comes from «invitar».
p.vino.consejo: The v sounds like b: BI-no. It is masculine: «el vino». Do not confuse it with «vino» from «venir».
p.jugoso.consejo: It comes from «jugo». The j sounds h: hu-GO-so.
p.llenas.consejo: Feminine plural of «lleno». The ll sounds y: YE-nas. It agrees with «copas».
p.hecha.consejo: Feminine of «hecho», participle of «hacer». The h is silent: E-cha. «Muy hecha» is well cooked.
p.poner.consejo: The stress is at the end: po-NER. In «yo» it is irregular: «pongo».
